subject: ACME DPA: subprocessor telemetry carveout and operational data use - action plan
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-25 09:12 -0700
Subject: ACME DPA redlines (telemetry + subprocessors)

Priya — attaching our third pass on the DPA. Two asks that we need clarity on before we can move: 1) a carveout that allows ACME to receive aggregated telemetry (latency, token counts, error rates) tied to our customer identifiers for billing reconciliation; 2) a tighter subprocessor clause so we can require notification and approval for any analytics vendor that receives telemetry derived from our traffic.

We redlined language on sections 4.2 and 7.1 (see pages 3–4). We are open to a scoped exception for aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry but need written commitments around retention windows and an explicit list of vendors that will receive exports. Please advise next steps and who on your side evaluates this operationally.

Attachments: ACME_DPA_redline_v3.pdf

—Jordan

Senior Counsel, ACME Health

PFA ACME's redlines. From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-25 13:22 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME DPA redlines (telemetry + subprocessors) — product impact

Short answer: we can support an aggregated telemetry export with constraints, but there are product trade-offs to call out.

Key points: 
- What they call "aggregated telemetry" needs to be scoped — is it per-tenant hourly aggregates, request-level metrics with tenant id, or only rolled-up daily snapshots? We should offer 3 tiers (real-time per-tenant metrics for billing — paid add-on; daily aggregates with 24h delay for ops; monthly rollups for long-term trends).
- Pseudonymization: we can hash tenant identifiers and drop PII fields before export. That limits debugging fidelity (stack traces + prompt snippets won't be included).
- Retention: we can enforce a max retention of 90 days for exported telemetry in analytics vendors; shorter (30 days) if it's cross-border.
- Vendor approvals: product can add a contractual requirement and a notif/approve flow, but runtime exports are currently implemented via our telemetry pipeline which fans out to configured outputs. Adding per-customer approval gating is a moderate engineering effort (Q3 sprint) unless we accept a limited workaround: maintain an allowlist of approved vendors per account and require manual ops approval for any new vendor during onboarding.

From a go-to-production perspective, the workable compromise is: hashed tenant ids, daily aggregates for default, 90-day retention cap, and an account-level allowlist with manual approvals for vendor additions. If Legal/Sales need real-time per-tenant streaming for billing accuracy, we'd need a separate paid integration and a security review.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr PM, Platform

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-25 16:40 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME DPA redlines (telemetry + subprocessors) — security assessment

Thanks for the context. Security's position: we can accept an explicit, narrow telemetry export for aggregated, pseudonymized metrics under the following mandatory controls: 
1) Data minimization: exports must contain no prompt/response text, no customer user ids, only hashed tenant ids and numeric metrics.
2) Retention limits: enforceable retention policy (TTL) @ 90 days by default; 30 days for EU/treated data.
3) Vendor onboarding: require a documented vendor security questionnaire (SOC2 or equivalent) and runtime allowlist. Ops must sign off on new vendor entries.
4) Access controls & encryption: exports must be encrypted in transit and at rest; keys must be customer- or Redwood-managed per the contract (prefer customer-managed KMS for high-risk accounts).
5) Audit & revocation: ability to revoke vendor access and to produce audit logs showing when exports were sent and to whom.

If Legal wants an explicit clause for "approval" we can accept language that requires Redwood to provide a vendor list and to obtain written approval for any vendor not on that list within the initial onboarding period; after that, new vendors require a 7-business-day review window and Ops sign-off.

I don't see a hard security blocker as long as we maintain the above controls and treat billing-grade per-request exports as a separate product (with elevated review).

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Product Security

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-26 15:34 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME DPA redlines (telemetry + subprocessors) — proposed compromise

Jordan — thanks for the redlines and for your patience while we reviewed. Proposed path forward (short and binding):

1) We will agree contractually to provide aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry exports scoped to numeric metrics (latency, token counts, error rates) with tenant hash only; no prompt/response content will be exported.
2) Retention: 90 days default for US accounts; 30 days for EU accounts — retention enforced by policy and auditable logs.
3) Subprocessor / vendor approvals: Redwood will provide an initial vendor allowlist at signing. For vendors not on the allowlist, Redwood will request written approval; Redwood will not onboard a new vendor without Ops sign-off. New vendor requests will follow a 7-business-day review cadence. ACME may request SOC2-equivalent evidence from any vendor.
4) If ACME requires per-request, real-time tenant-level streams for billing reconciliation, we will evaluate as a separate paid integration subject to security review and additional contractual terms.

If this matches ACME's needs, Legal: please revert with confirmation and we will prepare a narrow addendum to the DPA that captures these points. Once we have ACME confirmation, Security will approve and Legal can finalize redlines.

Next steps: Jordan — can you confirm if the allowlist + 7-business-day approval process is acceptable? If yes, we'll draft the addendum and attach the telemetry matrix (attached).

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
